clue.text: Only part of the problem is eg the fibre-optic, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that a fibre-optic cable is only a small part of what is going wrong with a network.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the visible top of a mostly submerged mass, so a small sign of a much larger difficulty.

clue.text: In part of ship, breakfast food served around wrong time of day?

indicators.note: the bread is served wrapped round the other piece, placing it inside

parts.note: toast is a breakfast staple
PM, the afternoon, is the wrong time for breakfast

explanation.surface: A sailor complains of being served breakfast at the wrong hour somewhere on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong time of day?' is a cryptic pointer to PM: afternoon is the wrong time for breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is the spar fixed above the lower mast on a sailing vessel, a component of the ship.

clue.text: Type that's confused about way in mountain track

indicators.note: about means the jumbled type is placed around the road

parts.note: pie (or pi) is printers' term for type that has been jumbled up
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A puzzled typist asks for directions to a path in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE is printers' jargon for a heap of muddled type, so 'confused' here belongs to the leaf, not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared ski run on a mountainside, a kind of track.

clue.text: Be transported by a cigar, strange hallucinogen

parts.note: to fly is to be carried through the air

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of the words a cigar are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is carried away by a peculiar cigar, suggesting it holds a mind-altering drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white toadstool contains psychoactive compounds and causes hallucinations when eaten.

clue.text: Jump round ring; shouldn't one jump through it?

indicators.note: round means the leap goes around the circle, holding it inside

parts.note: to hop is to jump
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A circus act: something leaps around a ring, but shouldn't it be leaping through it?
explanation.definitionFit: Circus animals and performers famously leap through a hoop, the cryptic description of the ring.

clue.text: One seabird in trap where people surf?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the bird inside the snare

parts.note: a net is a trap
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird caught in a net, in a seaside scene with surfers.
explanation.definitionFit: Online users are said to surf the web, browsing from page to page, rather than riding waves.

clue.text: Fix smart girl and yours truly up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a fashionable young woman entering society
the setter refers to themself, ME

explanation.surface: A request to set up a date between a fashionable girl and the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly within a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Is ready to edit royal film

indicators.note: editing rearranges material, so the letters of Is ready are reordered

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty

explanation.surface: A royal film is ready for the editors.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is a 1969 road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.

clue.text: Wine-producing area has some striking iron deposits

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wine region boasts remarkable reserves of iron ore.
explanation.definitionFit: The French department around Bordeaux is one of the world's great wine regions.

clue.text: Act timidly as cat's-paw

definitions.meaning: to tread warily and avoid committing oneself
literally the foot of a pussy-cat

explanation.surface: Behaving nervously in the manner of someone else's dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to behave cautiously; split in two, it is the paw of a cat.

clue.text: Lower barrier enclosing empty space

indicators.note: enclosing means the barrier wraps round what follows

parts.note: a bar is a barrier

indicators.note: empty means take away the inside, keeping only the first and last letters of space

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop a barrier round a vacant area.
explanation.definitionFit: Baser, more base, is the comparative meaning lower in rank or morality.

clue.text: In method of access, university going for good pay back here

indicators.note: the good letter goes in place of the university letter

parts.note: an avenue is a way of approach

explanation.surface: An academic route to getting one's money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to retaliate, paying the wrongdoer back for it.

clue.text: Benefit includes free new playing field

indicators.note: includes means the benefit holds the next piece

parts.note: a giro was a UK state benefit payment by cheque
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A benefit payment funds a free new sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A GIRO is a British benefit cheque, once the usual form of unemployment pay.
explanation.definitionFit: An American football field is nicknamed for its grid of yard lines.

clue.text: Sound quality of wood finally being turned

indicators.note: only the final pair of letters of the wood word are flipped round

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: How wood sounds once it has been worked on a lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of TIMBER are turned, ER becoming RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another.

clue.text: Addict under control in a month

indicators.note: in places the phrase for being controlled inside the month

parts.note: MAR is short for March
in line means behaving as directed

explanation.surface: A drug user has been kept in check for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a heroin user who injects into a vein.

clue.text: Head of BBC wearing curious sleeve that shouldn't unravel

indicators.note: the scrambled sleeve is worn by the head, enclosing it
curious signals that the letters of sleeve are rearranged

parts.note: the BBC's chief is the Director General, DG

explanation.surface: The BBC chief's odd sleeve is meant to hold together.
explanation.definitionFit: The woven edge of a fabric is finished so that it will not fray.

clue.text: Opposed to solitary confinement, ignoring small infringement

parts.note: V, versus, means against

indicators.note: ignoring means the small letter is left out

parts.note: isolation is solitary confinement

explanation.surface: A prison campaigner objects to solitary confinement, overlooking a minor breach.
explanation.definitionFit: A violation is a breach of a rule or law.

clue.text: Pointer the continental snake tailed

parts.note: LA is the French for the

indicators.note: tailed means the last letter is docked

parts.note: a serpent is a snake

explanation.surface: A pointer resembling a European snake with its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenters use a beam device to point at slides on a screen.

clue.text: Rabbit's little problem: caught by predator

indicators.note: the problem is caught inside the predator

parts.note: a cat is a predator
a hitch is a minor snag

explanation.surface: A rabbit's minor trouble: it has been seized by a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to rabbit (from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk) is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang sense: idle talk, gossip and natter.

clue.text: Nick is landed with hard work

parts.note: to cop something is to receive it, often unwillingly
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
OP, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick is lumbered with heavy labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang names for a police station.

clue.text: No time for wildly enjoyable event about to be hosted by prize solver

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are about to be held inside the prize

parts.note: a pot is a prize or jackpot

no means the time letter is dropped

parts.note: a riot is a hugely enjoyable occasion

explanation.surface: A wild party is lost to lack of time while a prize-winning puzzler hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize solver' reads as a competition winner, but the prize is wordplay; 'wildly' scrambles what 'No' leaves to IRO, tucked in by 'about to be hosted by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's detective is famous for solving crimes, a crossword-style sense of solver.

clue.text: Greek hero seen oddly in America

indicators.note: in places the odd letters inside the country

parts.note: the US is America

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of seen

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek is spotted at odd moments in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian hero of myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Top up, backing partner to drink litre

backing means the word up is read backwards

parts.note: a lover is a partner

explanation.surface: Topping up a drink, supporting a partner who downs a litre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullover is a knitted garment worn on the upper body, a top.

clue.text: Surprised reaction about publication in market town

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the publication

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
a mag, magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a magazine about a small market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone in Northern Ireland, with a market.

clue.text: With unfulfilled potential, chap starts to question universal education

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A man who never lived up to his promise starts questioning universal schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French: describes someone who failed to become what they might have been.

clue.text: Throwing game drops ball and walks out

indicators.note: drops means the ball-shaped letter is let go

parts.note: quoits is a game of throwing rings
O is ball-shaped

explanation.surface: A player drops the ball during a throwing game and storms off.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to leave; someone who quits a job walks out on it.

clue.text: Queen boards large sailing ship

indicators.note: boards means the Queen gets on, into the middle of large

parts.note: big means large
R, Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch steps aboard a big sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged vessel.

clue.text: Report of British members losing way in German League

indicators.note: losing means the road letters are taken out

parts.note: Hansard is the official record of debates by MPs in the UK Parliament
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: Parliament's record goes missing somewhere in a German league table.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanseatic League was a medieval association of north German trading towns.

clue.text: A guilty man, I cried uncontrollably after charge withdrawn

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the charge
withdrawn means the charge is pulled back, read in reverse

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge

indicators.note: uncontrollably signals that the letters of I cried are scrambled

explanation.surface: A defendant sobs helplessly after the case is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A parricide is one who has murdered a parent, certainly a guilty man.

clue.text: Book on unfinished temple has unusual origin

indicators.note: in an across clue, on puts the book after the temple
unfinished means the last letter is cut

parts.note: the Parthenon is the temple on the Acropolis
Genesis is the first book of the Bible
